_source: Rockwell 1606-XLS120E power supply, recorded product page. Title `XLS Power Supply 120W 24VDC 5A`. Values VERIFIED in the page: `620 g` ×3, `IP20` ×3, `100...240` ×3 (input voltage), `1.4A` ×3 (input current).
_tier: value-verified. The highest-yield HTML fixture in the corpus, chosen for promotion precisely because a high yield is where GARBAGE hides — the opposite failure mode from the low-yield fixtures.

_notes.raw_markup: This fixture found P1.3d. `splitNameValue` splits on `=`, and an HTML tag is full of `=`, so tags that reach the text layer were torn into label/value pairs: `<details id` = `"ra-product-new__documentation-table-mobile" class=…`, `<ra-footer origin="https` = `//www.rockwellautomation.com" …`, plus `<select`, `<textarea` and HTML COMMENTS (`<!-- <div class=…`). stripHtmlMarkup could not help: the splitter had already cut the tag, so no closing `>` remained to recognise. They are rejected on shape instead.
_notes.form_chrome: Same page: `Environmental compliance inquiry …` = `Business Email Address* This field is required Company Name* …` — a contact form parsed as a specification. A form asks for input; a datasheet states facts.
_notes.measured: 230 → 172 attributes (58 pieces of noise removed) with all 8 normalized fields unchanged — the noise was pure overhead, not a source of any value.
_notes.known_remaining: `Certification = Rockwell Automation N.V Pegasus Park De Kleet` is a company ADDRESS read as a certification (see P1.3e). It stays out of normalized.certificates (which is correctly `RCM`) but still reaches the Attributes sheet. Not asserted here yet — it is a separate, narrower fix in the certificate token allowlist.
_notes.output_current: normalized.current is `5 A @ 24 V / -6 A @ 24 V / -3 A @ 24 V` — several rated outputs joined. Not asserted: it is plausible for a multi-rating power supply but not verified, and the harness must never encode a guess as ground truth.
